# Inventory: the person's own items in your page

A person keeps an **inventory** of **items**. An item has one **kind**. The
kinds are `vehicle`, `character` and `image`. Your page says which kinds it accepts, in **slots**.
In each slot, `window.mindblown` (here `mb`) gives you the item this person chose, or
`null`. When you get `null`, draw your own default.

The same item fills the same kind of slot on every page that accepts it. So a
car a person makes or picks drives in your page and in other pages too.

## Declare the slots: `slots.json`

Put one file beside your entry page:

```json
{
  "car": {
    "kind": "vehicle", "versions": [1],
    "own": [
      { "id": "red", "name": "Red racer", "icon": "assets/red.png" },
      { "id": "van", "name": "Blue van", "icon": "assets/van.png" }
    ]
  }
}
```

- The slot name and the kind match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,39}$`.
- `kind` is required: `vehicle`, `character` or `image`.
- `versions` is optional.
- `own` is optional: **your page's own things** for this slot. The picker shows
  them first, under your page's title. They are not platform items: you draw
  them, so they need no file contract. `id` matches `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,39}$`,
  `name` is 1 to 40 characters, and `icon` is a picture your page serves (PNG,
  JPEG or WebP, a path beside your page). At most 24.
- `quality` is optional: `"simple"` (the default) or `"high"`. See below.
- A slot that is not in `slots.json` is refused with `UNKNOWN_SLOT`.

## The quality is your page's

Say what your page needs, and we serve and build to it:

```json
{ "car": { "kind": "vehicle", "quality": "high" } }
```

- **`simple`**: a light model (about 1.2 MB, 45k triangles). Right for most pages.
- **`high`**: modelled wheels with rims, discs and calipers, real glass, lit lamps
  (about 1.5 MB, 90k triangles). For a page that shows the car close up.
- A `high` slot gets the high model under the usual names: `files.glb` is the
  high model and `vehicle` holds its facts. Your code does not change.
- A `high` slot never gets an item that has no high model: `get` answers `null`
  (draw your own), and the picker and `shared(kind, { quality: "high" })` do
  not offer it.
- When the bot makes a car for your page, it builds the quality your slot
  declares.
- A `character` follows the same rule: a `high` slot gets its high model as
  `files.glb` and its facts under `character`.

## The calls

```js
const car = await mb.items.get("car");      // an item, { own: "red" }, or null
const choice = await mb.items.pick("car");   // OUR picker over your page
const off = mb.items.on("car", (car) => {}); // the person chose again
const all = await mb.items.shared("vehicle"); // the cars every page may offer
await mb.items.equip("car", all[0].id);       // this page; anybody may choose a shared item
await mb.items.equip("car", all[0].id, { everywhere: true }); // every page
await mb.items.equip("car", { own: "red" });  // one of your page's own
await mb.items.equip("car", null);            // clear this page's choice
```

| Call | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `get(slot)` | an item, `{ own: "<id>" }` (one of your page's own), or `null`. It does not fail when the panel is away; it answers `null` |
| `on(slot, fn)` | calls `fn` with the same shapes after an `equip` from this page and after a sign-in or sign-out. Returns the unsubscribe |
| `shared(kind, { quality })` | the shared items of that kind, newest first. Anybody may read them. With `quality`, only those with that model, under the usual names |
| `pick(slot)` | opens the platform's own picker over your page and waits. Answers `{ picked: item }`, `{ picked: { own: "<id>" } }`, or `{ cancelled: true }` when the person closed it. The choice is for this page only, and `on` listeners hear it too |
| `keep(sha, "image", { name })` | makes a picture that `mb.generate.image` made for this person an `image` item in their inventory, and answers the item. See [`image` v1](#image-v1) |
| `equip(slot, id, { own } or null, { everywhere })` | stores the person's choice and answers the new `get`. Anybody may choose a shared item or one of your page's own. Only a signed-in person may choose an item they own (`ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` otherwise). `{ own }` is for this page only, and only an id your `slots.json` declares (`UNKNOWN_OWN` otherwise). `null` clears this page's choice |

**`pick` is the easy way.** Your page draws no picker of its own: put one
button on your page and let us draw the choice. The person sees three sections:
your page's own things, their own items, and everyone's. A person who is not
signed in can sign in from the card. You get only the one they chose.

```js
document.querySelector("#change-car").onclick = async () => {
  const answer = await mb.items.pick("car");
  if (answer.cancelled) return;                          // they closed the card
  if (answer.picked.own) useMyOwnCar(answer.picked.own);  // one of yours, by its id
  else loadCar(answer.picked.files.glb.url, answer.picked.vehicle);
};
```

**One of your own beats the every-page choice.** A person who chose a car for
every page and then picks one of yours here gets yours on your page. That is how
a person goes back to your car.

**`null` means "draw your own default".** A person who chose nothing for
this kind gets `null`.

**Somebody not signed in can still choose a shared item.** Their choice is kept
in their browser and follows them to every page in that browser. It is not on
their account: after a sign-in, `get` answers the account's choice.

**Your page reads one item per slot.** It never sees the person's whole
inventory, and it never learns why a slot is empty.

## An item

```json
{
  "id": "8d1c5c1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000000",
  "kind": "vehicle",
  "version": 1,
  "name": "Pebble",
  "shared": true,
  "files": {
    "glb":  { "sha256": "<64 hex>", "bytes": 1843201, "type": "model/gltf-binary", "url": "/__mb/items/<sha256>.glb" },
    "icon": { "sha256": "<64 hex>", "bytes": 40211, "type": "image/png", "url": "/__mb/items/<sha256>.png" },
    "top":  { "sha256": "<64 hex>", "bytes": 61002, "type": "image/png", "url": "/__mb/items/<sha256>.png" },
    "side": { "sha256": "<64 hex>", "bytes": 58810, "type": "image/png", "url": "/__mb/items/<sha256>.png" }
  },
  "vehicle": {
    "min": [-0.92, 0.0, -2.21], "max": [0.92, 1.41, 2.23],
    "wheels": [[0.75, 0.36, 1.34], [-0.75, 0.36, 1.34], [0.74, 0.39, -1.34], [-0.74, 0.39, -1.34]],
    "wheelR": [0.36, 0.36, 0.39, 0.39]
  }
}
```

**The files load only on the published page.** Each `url` is a path on your
page's own address, named by the file's hash, and it never changes. Load it as
it is. Do not copy the file into your page.

## `vehicle` v1

Every vehicle obeys these rules, so your code can place any of them.

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| units and axes | metres; Y up; the front faces **+Z**; the vehicle's own left is +X |
| ground | every wheel touches y = 0 |
| `wheels` | 4 centres: front-left, front-right, rear-left, rear-right. Front z is larger than rear z. Left x > 0, right x < 0 |
| `wheelR` | 4 radii, in the same order |
| `min`, `max` | the box around the whole model. Length 1.5 to 8 m, width 0.8 to 3 m |
| `glb` | glTF 2.0 binary, at most 8 MiB and 200,000 triangles. It can use `EXT_meshopt_compression`, so set a Meshopt decoder on your loader. No Draco |
| wheel nodes | optional. When present they are `wheel_fl`, `wheel_fr`, `wheel_rl`, `wheel_rr` and turn about their own X axis, so you can spin them |
| `icon` | PNG, 256 x 256, three-quarter view from the front-left |
| `top` | PNG from above, the front up the picture, for a page drawn from above |
| `side` | PNG from the right side, the front to the right, for a page drawn from the side |

If your own models face -Z, turn an item 180 degrees about Y.

## `character` v1.1

A figure your page moves: a player, a rival, a guide. Declare it like any slot:

```json
{ "player": { "kind": "character" } }
```

**You play a clip by its name, and you never name a bone.** Every character
carries `idle`, `walk` and `run`. Its skeleton can be any skeleton, so do not
retarget your own clips onto its bones.

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| units and axes | metres; Y up; the character faces **+Z**; its own left is +X |
| ground | the feet stand on y = 0 |
| `height` | from 0.3 to 4 m, the rest pose's `max.y - min.y` |
| `min`, `max` | the box around the rest pose |
| `glb` | glTF 2.0 binary with one skeleton and a skinned mesh. At most 8 MiB and 100,000 triangles (a `high` slot's model: 200,000). It can use `EXT_meshopt_compression`, so set a Meshopt decoder on your loader. No Draco |
| clips, always | `idle`, `walk`, `run` |
| clips, sometimes | `jump`, `fall`, `land`, `punch`, `hurt`, `die`, `cheer` |
| fight clips, sometimes | `guard`, `step_in`, `step_out`, `jab`, `cross`, `hook`, `uppercut`, `block`, `hit_head`, `hit_body`, `knockout` |
| `clips` | the names this character carries. Check it before you play an optional clip |
| `icon` | PNG, 256 x 256, three-quarter view from the front-left, in the `idle` pose |

The facts are under `character`: `{ "height", "min", "max", "clips" }`, and
`motion` when the character carries any. `motion` is what you cannot see in a
clip, measured from it. Use it; a guess slides the feet and throws a punch
through the other figure's head.

| `motion.<clip>` | For | Means |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `speed` | `walk`, `run`, `step_in`, `step_out` | metres a second. The clip stays in place: move the figure at this speed while it plays, or the feet slide |
| `reach` | `punch`, `jab`, `cross`, `hook`, `uppercut` | metres in front of the figure's origin that the fist gets to. Stand the target's face this far away |
| `contact` | the same | seconds into the clip when the fist arrives. Start the hit reaction then |
| `hand` | the same | `left` or `right` |

```js
const m = item.character.motion || {};
// walk forward without sliding
if (m.walk) hero.position.addScaledVector(forward, m.walk.speed * dt);
// a jab that lands: close to m.jab.reach first, react at m.jab.contact
if (m.jab) setTimeout(() => rival.play("hit_head"), m.jab.contact * 1000);
```

## `image` v1

A picture the person made with `mb.generate.image` and kept. A charm box, a
jar of butterflies or a frame on a wall takes one in an `image` slot:

```json
{ "charm": { "kind": "image" } }
```

```js
const { url, sha } = await mb.generate.image(prompt);   // see generate.md
const kept = await mb.items.keep(sha, "image", { name: "Teal morpho" });
await mb.items.equip("charm", kept.id);                // this page's charm slot
const charm = await mb.items.get("charm");             // the kept picture, or null
```

| Rule | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `png` | the picture, PNG, from 64 to 2048 pixels on each side, at most 8 MiB |
| `icon` | PNG, 256 x 256: the picture fitted inside the square, centred, on a clear ground |
| `image` | `{ "width", "height" }` of `png` in pixels, so you can lay it out before it loads |

- `keep` needs a signed-in person who made the picture. Anybody else gets
  `ACCOUNT_REQUIRED` or a not-found refusal.
- `name` is from 1 to 60 characters.
- Keeping the same picture again answers the same item.

## Example: put the person's car in a three.js scene

```js
import { GLTFLoader } from "./vendor/GLTFLoader.js";
import { MeshoptDecoder } from "./vendor/meshopt_decoder.module.js";

const loader = new GLTFLoader().setMeshoptDecoder(MeshoptDecoder);
let car = null;

async function show(item) {
  if (car) scene.remove(car);
  if (!item) { car = myDefaultCar(); scene.add(car); return; } // null: your own car
  const gltf = await loader.loadAsync(item.files.glb.url);
  car = gltf.scene;
  car.userData.wheels = item.vehicle.wheels; // for your physics and your camera
  scene.add(car);
}

show(await mb.items.get("car"));
mb.items.on("car", show);
```

## Example: a character that walks and runs

```js
import * as THREE from "./vendor/three.module.js";
import { GLTFLoader } from "./vendor/GLTFLoader.js";
import { MeshoptDecoder } from "./vendor/meshopt_decoder.module.js";

const loader = new GLTFLoader().setMeshoptDecoder(MeshoptDecoder);
let hero = null, mixer = null, clips = {}, playing = null;

async function show(item) {
  if (hero) scene.remove(hero);
  if (!item) { hero = myDefaultHero(); scene.add(hero); mixer = null; return; } // null: your own
  const gltf = await loader.loadAsync(item.files.glb.url);
  hero = gltf.scene;
  mixer = new THREE.AnimationMixer(hero);
  clips = {};
  for (const clip of gltf.animations) clips[clip.name] = mixer.clipAction(clip);
  playing = null;
  play("idle");
  scene.add(hero);
}

// Cross-fade to a clip by its name. An optional clip may be missing:
// item.character.clips says which ones this character has.
function play(name) {
  const next = clips[name];
  if (!next || next === playing) return;
  next.reset().play();
  if (playing) playing.crossFadeTo(next, 0.2, false);
  playing = next;
}

const clock = new THREE.Clock();
function frame() {
  const dt = clock.getDelta();
  if (mixer) mixer.update(dt);
  play(speed > 4 ? "run" : speed > 0.1 ? "walk" : "idle");
  renderer.render(scene, camera);
  requestAnimationFrame(frame);
}

show(await mb.items.get("player"));
mb.items.on("player", show);
frame();
```
